segments.text: Welcome back to GitHub awesome. This is GitHub trending today number 53. 35 trending open- source projects on GitHub right now. Let's get into it.
Omari Apple-Dev lets you build Swift UI and Flutter iPhone apps from Omar Linux, then install them on a real iPhone over
USB. There's no Mac OS or Xcode installation in the workflow, though the full setup still needs Apple's Xcode
download for its iOS SDK. It also packages and validates apps for test flight or the app store with a paid
Apple developer account required for those releases.
Replica skill is 11 clawed skills for building your own take on an existing app. It maps the screens and user flows,
plans the back end, builds and tests the result, then compares what's missing.
One clever step reads linked user reviews to find complaints your version could address. The workflow uses public
information or your own account, writes fresh code, and requires new branding before launch.
REIA gives coding agents a way to investigate software when the source code isn't available. It connects through MCP to inspect native binaries,
Electron apps, Android packages, websites, and more. Then returns evidence your agent can follow up on.
Ask how a feature works, and the agent can trace the relevant pieces before building its own version. The analysis runs locally with GIDRA, Hopper or IDA needed for deeper native work.
Big arrow on the screen solves a tiny but familiar AI agent problem. It needs you to click something and its message is buried in a terminal. On a Mac, the
agent can draw a labeled arrow, ring, or box over the exact control you need. Your clicks still reach the app.
Keyboard focus stays put and the pointer disappears on its own. It's a simple visual handoff for permissions, setup, and step-by-step help.
FS search is a Mac OS command line search tool for that file you know exists but can't quite name. It indexes the disk, forgives typos, and searches
inside text files with filters for folder, type, size, and date. The author reports a median 1.3 milliseconds for
name searches across 7.7 million files on an M4 Max. A small Damon keeps the index current as files change.
Omdrop Owl brings AirDrop to Linux machines that don't have Apple's Wi-Fi chip. It's the radio half of Omdrop
built on Owl, a user space reimplementation of Apple's ADDL protocol. The trick is keeping your Wi-Fi connected while AirDrop runs on
the same channel by injecting frames from the station's MAC and letting it act the phone's traffic so you can send
and receive from an iPhone without dropping your network.
West Boss took two locked down Android picture frames, a skylight calendar and a BYU frame and turned them into proper
dashboards. The repo logs how he got ADB, backed up the firmware, rooted them, pulled out the vendor app, and ran his own launcher and kiosk on the
Skylight. Root came from adding one file to the boot RAM disc. The guide is written partly for AI agents as a
nine-phase map an agent can follow over USB.
AI homepage replaces Chrome's new tab with a homepage an AI agent writes for you from your own browsing. It ranks the
sites you visit most, opens up to eight of them in a background window signed in as you, pulls out the headlines and links, then writes a single React component that becomes your new tab.
Tell it what you want in plain English, a morning newspaper or a green on black terminal, and it rebuilds on a timer.
Helix Foundry is a local data workspace that connects your company's scattered tools, Postgress, Stripe, Postthog, S3,
and more. Then proposes one connected ontology across all of them. It snapshots your data as version parquet, queries it with duct DB, and stores the
relationships in Helix DB. Ask the analyst a question, and it answers with the SQL it actually ran, citing the snapshot.
OSS Scanner is Anthropic's free service that hunts for security bugs in open-source projects and maintainers
sign up with a single pull request. You add a folder with a config file and a Docker file, plus an optional threat model describing what you actually care
about. The scanner builds your project in an isolated VM, then cuts its internet access before it starts looking.
CCode lets Claude and other coding agents draw proper diagrams without ever writing SVG themselves. The agent writes
a short JSON spec of what connects to what and CCO handles the layout, edge routing, labels, and animation, then outputs one self-contained HTML file.
There are 42 diagram types from architecture and sequence to seni and wardly maps.
Speak rail is a fully local voice assistant that listens while it talks running on one RTX 4090. You can cut it
off mid-sentence, say m without it stopping, or pause to think without it jumping in. Every 80 milliseconds, a
small turnt head decides whether you're done, pausing, or just back channeling.
And Gemma picks speak, listen, or yield in about one token.
Finder search is what happens when a lightning fast file name search engine gets a familiar Mac interface. Start typing even with a typo and it finds
matching files across your disc. From there you can browse in columns, icons, lists or a gallery. Preview with quick
look and handle files without opening another app. It uses F search under the hood. Keep searches on your Mac.
FF tracking is the source for a six-second motion graphic that makes an AI agent's terminal look like it's being filmed by a restless camera. A tracker
follows the letters as they appear. The focus shifts with it, and each lock gets a synthesized beep. There's no recorded
footage or stock audio. The screen, camera effects, and sounds all come from code. Change the text or camera moves, then render your own version.
Jackson Lint checks GitHub actions workflows before a broken or risky one reaches CI. It catches bad YAML keys,
mistyped expressions, wrong action inputs, and scripts that drop untrusted text straight into a shell command. It
also flags issues like overly broad permissions, and unpinned actions. Run it across a repo, use its suggested fixes, or set a baseline so an existing project only fails on new problems.
Strandsbox is a sandbox for running AI agents with two layers of control. The OS walls off files and programs and a
policy language called Dogwood decides every shell command, Python call, network request, and MCP tool call with
everything denied unless a rule permits it. Because the gateways share a history, a policy can say once the agent has read a secrets file, block its next outbound request.
Good CSS is a set of modern CSS habits packaged for coding agents with a live example for each one. It nudges an agent
toward fluid sizing with clamp color tokens that handle light and dark modes and layouts that adapt without piles of breakpoints or JavaScript. Each practice
says when to use it and shows the actual CSS so the advice can fit a plain stylesheet, tailwind or another setup.
AI data extractor pulls your chat history out of 10 AI coding assistants, claude code, codecs, cursor, and more
into one normalized JSONL format. It finds where each tool stores its chats on Mac, Linux, or Windows, reads SQLite
databases readon, so a running editor isn't blocked, and keeps the code context, diffs, and tool calls alongside each message.
Absent author gives researchers and reviewers a way to check whether anyone really stood behind a paper. Its two agent skills help authors map claims to
evidence and help reviewers find concrete problems like references that don't exist or numbers that change between tables. A separate llinter flags writing patterns for human inspection.
The important restraint polished pros or an AI looking phrase is never treated as proof of research.
Open intelligent UI is an open recreation of chat GPT's interactive answers. Ask for a one-day San Francisco plan and you don't get a wall of text.
You get a map, photos, and an itinerary you can edit. Pins drop onto the map while the answer streams. Then the route
draws in once it finishes. Remove a stop or add a suggestion and your edits go back to the model on the next turn. Once
is for commands whose output you need again, but don't want to fetch again.
wrap a command, set an expiry, and later calls reuse its output from a small background process. The handy example is
reading a one password token. Approve it with your fingerprint once, then keep using it for the next few hours. Cached
values stay in memory, and the process exits when they expire.
Purable kit lets an iPhone or Mac app run AI agents that survive being killed.
It wraps the PI durable agent library and runs it in JavaScript core behind a native Swift API, writing every conversation, model turn, and tool call
to storage before the UI shows it. So when iOS kills your app mid turn, you reopen it and the agent carries on from where it stopped.
Isoigure is a clawed skill that draws a working isometric object in a single HTML file. Ask for a kitchen timer or a
light switch and you get a fine line technical drawing on a numbered plate where the buttons actually do something when you press them. It's plain SVG with
no libraries. About 15 lines of projection code put every face on its isometric plane.
Antibbody tackles a familiar problem when you run several coding agents. They all hit the same error and each spends time solving it. It recognizes matching
failures across work trees, lets one agent claim the diagnosis, then passes its recorded fix to the others. The shared memory lives with the repo and it
works with claude code, Gemini CLI, and Codeex CLI. One fix, fewer agents stuck on the same wall.
VB6 Studio Web brings the classic Visual Basic workflow into your browser. You can lay out forms, edit VB style code,
run it, step through it in a debugger, and export a project as a standalone HTML app. It can also open original VB6
project files. This is a browser implementation with compatibility limits, but it's a surprisingly hands-on way to explore and adapt old Visual Basic projects.
Liquid Glass brings that glassy refracting look to React and the web with real live refraction rendered on the GPU through web GPU. You get two
materials, clear, which is fully transparent, and regular, which is frosted. Both come in light and dark.
Wrap your surfaces, buttons, toolbars, tabs, and menus in a glass scene, and they bend whatever sits behind them. Ref
2 game is a skill for turning a reference image into a playable 2D game prototype. Give Claude code or codeex a
screenshot and it guides the agent through matching the art, building a browser game, and adding movement, lighting, and effects in code. You can
play the work in progress, point out what feels wrong, and get a static build with the source and assets.
Bigwords.page puts your message full screen in giant text that fits any display with nothing else on the page.
Type it in the editor and the whole message lives in the link itself. after the hash, which browsers never send to the server. So there's no backend, no
account, and nothing stored. Separate slides with two pipes add a countdown to a date or drop in a QR code for your Wi-Fi.
Tracemaker takes a Kyad circuit board with unfinished connections and draws the tracks and VAS for you. It can also
move components to make a board easier to route. And there's a live viewer so you can watch the paths appear. The useful check is Kyad's own design rules, not just the router saying it succeeded.
It runs on the CPU with optional GPU acceleration.
Lithos Metal is an open-source engine for running large language models locally on Apple Silicon. It builds
specialized Metal kernels to cut GPU overhead, then serves the model through APIs that coding agents can use. There
are launch commands for codeex, claude code, and open code. The current work centers on specific Quen models with
performance measured on selected Macs, so check its hardware list before trying it. Excaladraw CLI puts your drawings in
the terminal. You can render a local.exal file to a PNG without an account, which makes diagrams easy to generate in a script or attach to a
build. With an Excaladraw plus API key, it can also list, create, and edit scenes and collections in your
workspace. Commands return JSON by default, so coding agents can work with them, too.
Integer malt bounds asks a surprisingly deep question. How much faster can we multiply enormous integers? Contributors
are sharpening a mathematical bound built on an earlier open AAI research framework with proof arguments, exact certificates, and checks others can
rerun. The latest reviewed result improves the claimed bound, but it still depends on assumptions in that framework.
Habla turns your clawed code and codec sessions into a little pixel art office.
Each project gets a room and each agent becomes a character you can watch working, waiting on a command, or raising a hand when it needs you. Click
one to see its activity and session details. It runs locally, making a crowded set of agent tasks much easier to understand at a glance.
Trading Chart is a native Swift UI library for iOS trading charts built on Apple's Swift Charts. You get candlesticks, line, and area styles,
plus SMA, EMA, Ballinger bands, RSI, and MACD with a protocol for writing your own. Swift Charts draws the bars, while
lightweight canvas layers handle the axes, crosshair, and drawings. So, the chart isn't rebuilt on every scroll frame. Gentle Dot is a personal AI
assistant that lives on your Mac desktop, one key away. It keeps one continuous chat with long-term memory, reads your files, and can drive your
apps, seeing the screen, clicking, typing, and opening things. Each control session needs your approval. Risky
actions ask first. Password managers and system settings are off limits.
